NGFhc8R_uO4.summary: A HOPE09 talk on how modern computer chips are manufactured, from 22nm transistors to ultra-clean fabs and the tricks used to pattern tiny features with light. It frames chipmaking as hacking electrical engineering and physics.
NGFhc8R_uO4.why: HN repeatedly calls it the best in-depth introduction to IC manufacturing, a sense-of-awe talk by an independent engineer, while wishing for an updated version.

NNnIGh9g6fA.summary: The opening lecture of Robert Sapolsky's Stanford course on Human Behavioral Biology, explaining the course premise and how to avoid categorical thinking. It starts a roughly 25-lecture series on how biology, genes, hormones and environment shape behavior.
NNnIGh9g6fA.why: One of the most consistently recommended lecture series on HN, praised as fascinating, funny and eye-opening about human behavior across many scales.

NOAgplgTxfc.summary: Stanford professor Robert Sapolsky lectures on depression as a real biological disease. He covers its biological and psychological causes, how it differs from ordinary sadness, and ideas such as learned helplessness. He ties these together into one account.
NOAgplgTxfc.why: HN returns to it repeatedly as the best single introduction to understanding clinical depression.

NQFqDKRAROI.summary: Explains the proposed NASA JPL plan to use the Sun as a gravitational lens, sending solar sail craft to its focal region to image an exoplanet's surface. It covers the distances involved, how imaging with the Sun would work and the mission design.
NQFqDKRAROI.why: HN strongly recommends it as the clearest, best-illustrated explanation of the solar gravitational lens idea, and links it whenever exoplanet imaging comes up.

NVGuFdX5guE.summary: CGP Grey argues for picking a theme for the year or season instead of setting goals or new year's resolutions. He explains how a theme gives direction without a pass/fail target.
NVGuFdX5guE.why: A staple recommendation in new year and goal-setting threads, with many commenters adopting yearly themes.

N1pIYI5JQLE.summary: A short clip from a Richard Feynman interview in which he explains fire, describing how burning wood releases sunlight stored by the tree, which built itself mostly from air. It showcases his curiosity and plain-spoken explanations.
N1pIYI5JQLE.why: HN repeatedly cites it as an elegant, eye-opening explanation of fire and photosynthesis and as an example of Feynman's infectious love of knowledge.

Nb2tebYAaOA.summary: Lex Fridman interviews legendary chip architect Jim Keller about Moore's Law, microprocessor design, and first-principles thinking. Keller draws on his work at AMD, Apple, Tesla and Intel, discussing instruction sets, transistor budgets, and self-driving.
Nb2tebYAaOA.why: HN cites it whenever chip architecture, Moore's Law or CPU design comes up, as an unusually deep and accessible view from a top designer.

NdSD07U5uBs.summary: Alan Kay's 2015 talk on the power of simplicity, arguing that systems become simpler by building on more sophisticated fundamental building blocks and that big research horizons drove invention at Xerox PARC. It ranges across computing, tools and scaling software.
NdSD07U5uBs.why: HN repeatedly cites it as a thought-provoking talk on reducing software complexity and on the state of computing research.

N1CBDTgGtOU.summary: A five-minute lightning demo of VisiData, a terminal tool for exploring and manipulating data. It uses two months of NYC 311 complaint data to drill down, plot points on a virtual map and save selected rows.
N1CBDTgGtOU.why: HN recommends it as the fastest way to understand what VisiData can do, since seeing it work is clearer than reading about it.

NAsM30MAHLg.summary: The first of four short videos from Bill Hammack (engineerguy) introducing and giving the history of a 100-year-old mechanical computer, Michelson's harmonic analyzer. The series goes on to explain Fourier synthesis, analysis and operation of the machine.
NAsM30MAHLg.why: Commenters recommend the series whenever Fourier analysis or analog computing comes up, praising Hammack's clear explanations and the short episodes.

NdppYYfQJgg.summary: A 38C3 talk on how advanced chips are made, centered on EUV lithography and the global supply chain behind it. It covers technical challenges from raw materials to finished chips and the geopolitical weight of semiconductors.
NdppYYfQJgg.why: HN users recommend it as an excellent, accessible overview of how modern chips are produced and why EUV matters.

Nq2HkAYbG5o.summary: Damian Conway's hour-long keynote at the Perl conference, On the Shoulders of Giants, showing off Perl 6 (Raku) features with history, algorithms and a quantum math operator built with grammars. It is delivered with comic flair.
Nq2HkAYbG5o.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining, technically masterful showcase of what Perl 6 can do.

NH1Tta7purM.summary: Optiver's Carl Cook explains how to build high-frequency trading systems in C++, where the critical path runs rarely but must be extremely fast. He covers techniques for low and predictable latency, including avoiding main memory and cache misses.
NH1Tta7purM.why: HN repeatedly points people to it as the best overview of low-latency trading engineering.

NHopJHSlVo4.summary: A four-minute TED talk in which Derek Sivers argues that announcing your goals can make you less likely to achieve them. He cites psychology research going back to the 1920s.
NHopJHSlVo4.why: Commenters credit it with changing how they handle plans and recommend it as a short, sourced talk.

NRoUC9P1PmA.summary: Jeff Bonwick and Bill Moore, the creators of ZFS, present 'ZFS: The Last Word in File Systems' at the 2008 SNIA Software Developers' Conference. They explain the design, including copy-on-write, checksumming and avoiding the write hole.
NRoUC9P1PmA.why: HN recommends it as the definitive explanation of ZFS design straight from its inventors, with war stories about data integrity.

NVl9_6J1G60.summary: Dan Robinson, then CTO of Heap, explains how Heap runs its product analytics backend on PostgreSQL and CitusDB. It covers conversion funnels, retention and cohort queries across tens of billions of events and 50 TB of data, plus Postgres and Kafka together and the indexing strategy.
NVl9_6J1G60.why: HN commenters point to it as a first-hand overview of Heap's Postgres/Citus architecture and its distinctive indexing approach.

NlIdzF1_b5M.summary: Wendover Productions explains why Boeing's efficient 787 beat Airbus's giant A380, contrasting hub-and-spoke with point-to-point routes. It covers the economics of long-haul flights.
NlIdzF1_b5M.why: Recommended in threads on the 747 and A380 for explaining why big planes were phased out.

NWSZ4c9yqW8.summary: Simon Peyton Jones explains nested data parallelism and Data Parallel Haskell, an approach to exploiting multicore and distributed hardware while keeping a simple single-control-flow programming model.
NWSZ4c9yqW8.why: Recommended as a fascinating look at easy parallelism abstractions, though other commenters note the approach never beat sequential C by much.

N3bJnKmeNJY.summary: NightHawkInLight shows how to make ultra-white radiative paint that cools surfaces below ambient temperature without electricity. He walks through the research papers and the household-materials process.
N3bJnKmeNJY.why: HN points to it as a practical, well-researched DIY demonstration of passive radiative cooling.

NP9AIUT9nos.summary: Glenn Vanderburg argues at Lone Star Ruby Conference 2010 that university-style software engineering does not work, and asks what real software engineering would look like. He revisits the waterfall model and what engineering means in other fields.
NP9AIUT9nos.why: HN recommends it for changing minds about whether programmers can be called engineers, and for its take on how waterfall was misread.

NcOb3Dilzjc.summary: The first episode of James Burke's Connections series, 'The Trigger Effect', explores how modern society depends on interlinked technological systems and how quickly it breaks down when they fail, starting with a power blackout.
NcOb3Dilzjc.why: Recommended whenever outages and cascading failures come up, as a classic on interdependent systems.

Nrp_LZ-XGsY.summary: Scott Wlaschin demystifies functional programming terms like monads, monoids, functors and catamorphisms by showing how they fit into a small toolkit. He applies them to problems such as missing data, list handling, and functional dependency injection.
Nrp_LZ-XGsY.why: HN recommends it as the best beginner-friendly introduction to monoids, monads and other FP vocabulary.

N-yALPEpV4w.summary: Michael Shellenberger argues in a TEDx talk that solar and wind need huge amounts of land and mining, and says nuclear power is a better path to protecting both the climate and nature.
N-yALPEpV4w.why: HN commenters credit it with changing their minds on nuclear power and cite it for the downsides of renewables.

NKlbE2eROC0.summary: Modern Vintage Gamer examines the claim from the Super Mario 64 decompilation project that the game shipped unoptimized, and puts it in the context of 1996 N64 development.
NKlbE2eROC0.why: Recommended as a well-researched rebuttal of the idea that Nintendo simply forgot an optimization flag.

NMvwHDFVpCE.summary: A recording of Andres Duany's 1991 'San Antonio By Design' seminar on suburban sprawl. He lays out how codes, zoning and policy produce sprawl and makes the case for new urbanism.
NMvwHDFVpCE.why: HN recommends it as a comprehensive, still-accurate and often funny account of how zoning and policy force suburban sprawl.

NUQu-OPrzUc.summary: Russell Barkley gives the keynote at UNC's 2012 Burnett Seminar on ADHD. He presents it as an executive function disorder and discusses its effects and how to help.
NUQu-OPrzUc.why: HN recommends it as a rigorous clinical look at ADHD, including the view that it has no benefits and that external prompts help.

NXN7TOg3kj4.summary: The first lesson of MangoJelly's FreeCAD 0.20 beginner course, covering setup, preferences and navigation. The series teaches fundamentals through complete workflows such as sketching, Part Design and STL export.
NXN7TOg3kj4.why: HN recommends it as an excellent beginner series that fills FreeCAD's gap in learning material.

NYSgd1XSZXc.summary: Tourist footage of the 660-ton tuned mass damper in Taipei 101 swaying during tremors from the 2008 Sichuan earthquake. The damper hangs from the 92nd floor.
NYSgd1XSZXc.why: Recommended whenever skyscraper dampers come up, since it shows how huge the moving mass is.

NaL_Cb42WyY.summary: 3Blue1Brown shows how pi emerges from prime numbers via complex numbers and sums of squares, culminating in a formula for approximating pi.
NaL_Cb42WyY.why: Praised as a beautiful, understandable proof and a favorite among 3Blue1Brown videos.

N6xLMUifbxQ.summary: A panel at The National WWII Museum on the Battle of Kursk, moderated by Keith Huxen with historians Robert Citino and John Parshal. The discussion covers the armored engagement and the German, Soviet and US approaches to tank production.
N6xLMUifbxQ.why: HN recommends it for its comparison of tank factory efficiency and the Soviet approach of building cheap tanks with short lifespans.

NeopkvAP-ag.summary: A Technology Connections video essay on how analog and digital clocks shape different mental models of time, with the minute hand acting as a progress indicator.
NeopkvAP-ag.why: HN points to it whenever analog versus digital clocks come up, as an idea that changed how commenters think about time perception.

NiRrvxjrJ1U.summary: MIT's Donald Sadoway presents the liquid metal battery as a design for grid-scale stationary electricity storage, at an Imperial College London event in 2018. He covers the grid benefits of massive-scale storage.
NiRrvxjrJ1U.why: HN brings it up in energy storage threads as a promising scalable grid storage technology, and calls it worth the hour.

NngCHTImH1g.summary: A 20-minute S3 episode touring Terraform Industries, a startup making synthetic natural gas from air and solar power. It walks through the reactor, injection system, direct air capture and electrolyzer, plus the company's cost goals and next milestone.
NngCHTImH1g.why: HN commenters point to it as a clear, short tour of Terraform's synthetic fuel approach and goals.

Nnuq9PXbywA.summary: Organist Hans-Andre Stamm performs Bach's Toccata and Fugue in D minor, BWV 565, on the Trost organ in Waltershausen, Germany, an instrument from 1730. The video shows the playing and footwork.
Nnuq9PXbywA.why: Recommended as an expressive performance on a historically significant organ with good videography.

Npd_xDuNi9k.summary: Louis Rossmann gives a basic, non-technical introduction to right to repair legislation for people new to the issue.
Npd_xDuNi9k.why: Recommended as the accessible explanation to share with non-techies, family and politicians.

N4UFC0y1tY0.summary: At GDC 2019, Bennett Foddy and Zach Gage ask why game developers rarely sign their work. They argue that indie developers could benefit from putting their names on their games.
N4UFC0y1tY0.why: HN recommends it when people ask why games aren't marketed by creator like films, and for the value of attaching your name to your work.

N8elxpSu9pw.summary: Bisqwit writes a raytracer from scratch in C++ for DOS, rendering in the 16-color VGA palette at 640x480. The video also covers color quantization and ordered dithering.
N8elxpSu9pw.why: HN fans praise Bisqwit as a favorite programming YouTuber and this video as an excellent look at dithering.

N9RUqGYuGfw.summary: Tsoding live-codes a JSON parser from scratch in Haskell in about 111 lines, using only the standard library. It is an edited Twitch stream that explains the intuition behind parser combinators, functors, applicatives and monads.
N9RUqGYuGfw.why: HN recommends it as a hands-on way to understand Haskell and parser combinators by watching a parser get built live.

NAh9oLs67Cw.summary: An hour-long absurdist Lasagna Cat video in which John Blyth Barrymore muses philosophically on a single Garfield strip. It is set to the full score of Philip Glass's Kundun.
NAh9oLs67Cw.why: HN cites it as the prime example of going absurdly deep on a tiny subject, and as a favorite among long YouTube videos.

NbpZCSf4_Yk.summary: Digital Foundry's Alex Battaglia analyzes Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition, the first AAA game built around ray tracing. It covers the new global illumination, emissive lighting, DLSS and performance on AMD and Nvidia hardware.
NbpZCSf4_Yk.why: HN recommends it as a good overview of what ray-traced lighting changes for developers and players.

NfizT369g60.summary: Ubisoft procedural technical artist Etienne Carrier explains the Houdini-based tools used to build Far Cry 5's roughly 100 square km open world. It covers generating biomes, texturing terrain, freshwater networks, cliff rocks and vegetation placement.
NfizT369g60.why: HN points people to it as a rare, concrete look at how a AAA studio uses procedural tools to fill huge worlds with natural-looking environments.

N8SS-rUEZPg.summary: Paul Irish and Pavel Feldman present the newest Chrome Dev Tools features at Google I/O 2011, including live CSS editing, saving changes, breakpoints and network analysis. It also covers remote debugging.
N8SS-rUEZPg.why: In 2011 HN people cited it as a convincing introduction that won them over to Chrome's developer tools.

N9c7_8Gp7gI.summary: Alan Kay argues for rethinking how computer science is taught in schools, drawing on his work on object-oriented programming and GUIs. He discusses how poorly people understand complex systems and what education could do about it.
N9c7_8Gp7gI.why: HN readers cite Kay's talks for his views on programming languages as user interfaces, thinking beyond logic, and why people struggle with complex systems.

ND2TeNfcmKA.summary: A 1966 NASA safety film teaching workers how to handle toxic rocket propellants such as hydrazine and nitrogen tetroxide. It explains the hazards of these corrosive, flammable and toxic chemicals and what to do after contamination.
ND2TeNfcmKA.why: Commenters share it as a favorite vintage NASA film with a sobering look at how dangerous hypergolic propellants are.

NIu_dJGyIQI.summary: Neuroscientist Karl Friston gives a 15-minute talk on the free energy principle, covering Markov blankets, Bayesian model evidence and global brain theories.
NIu_dJGyIQI.why: Offered as a high-level, approachable introduction to Friston's idea of the brain as a prediction machine.

NK1zlz67MjU.summary: Chuck Moore, creator of Forth, gives his annual Fireside Chat at Forth Day 2011 at Stanford. He talks about his multi-core GreenArrays chip design and demonstrates code running on it.
NK1zlz67MjU.why: HN recommends it as a window into Moore's minimalist CPU design and the GA144 chip, despite the slow pace.

NTJQTc-TqpU.summary: A video tour of Magnasanti, a SimCity city built to hold six million residents, pushed to the absolute maximum and inspired by Kowloon Walled City.
NTJQTc-TqpU.why: Cited as the legendary extreme SimCity build, and recommended as fascinating viewing with the creator's commentary.

NmGaXEmfTIo.summary: Technology Connections takes apart a 1970 Wurlitzer 3400 jukebox to show how electromechanical relays and switches automated its behavior without a computer.
NmGaXEmfTIo.why: Recommended as an eye-opening look at pre-computer automation and relay logic.

Nsjsiz2A9mg.summary: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) talks about clean architecture and design, including keeping the database and frameworks out of the center of an application. It is an hour-long conference talk.
Nsjsiz2A9mg.why: Recommended as a formative talk on architecture that argues against putting the database at the center of a design.

N2jZryt607U.summary: FortNine surveys motorcycle airbag technology and explains why airbags have not reached mainstream adoption. It breaks down gear such as the Helite Turtle, Dainese D-Air and Alpinestars Tech-Air.
N2jZryt607U.why: Recommended in threads about airbag vests as a solid overview when shopping for a motorcycle airbag.

N65DpT2nqEI.summary: Big Clive shows how to pick up discarded disposable vape devices from the roadside and extract the rechargeable lithium cells inside. He explains why these devices contain the same circuitry as rechargeable ones and how to reuse the cells.
N65DpT2nqEI.why: Used as the explanation behind the free-lithium-cell scavenging idea in threads about vapes and battery reuse.

NBvbsPNBIyk.summary: The Computer History Museum's 25th anniversary celebration of the Commodore 64, recorded in December 2007, with a panel including Jack Tramiel and Steve Wozniak. It recounts the machine's launch and history.
NBvbsPNBIyk.why: HN links it for Jack Tramiel's pricing philosophy and a memorable Tramiel and Wozniak exchange on low versus sustainable pricing.

NM51qOpwcIM.summary: Footage of Stefani Germanotta, later Lady Gaga, performing 'Captivated' and 'Electric Kiss' at NYU's Ultraviolet Live talent show in 2005-era college days. It shows her singing and playing before she became famous.
NM51qOpwcIM.why: HN uses it to show that Lady Gaga is a genuinely skilled musician and writer of her own songs.

NPOHf20slZg.summary: Coffeezilla investigates the company behind the Rabbit R1 AI gadget, alleging a shady history as a crypto and NFT startup and questioning its large action model claims.
NPOHf20slZg.why: HN threads on the Rabbit R1 point to it as an exposé on the company's history and operation.

NST3u-GjjFw.summary: Jesse Newland describes how GitHub uses Hubot, its chat bot, to run operations such as deployment, monitoring, graphing and provisioning from chat rooms. He explains how this improves shared awareness and remote work culture.
NST3u-GjjFw.why: The go-to reference for ChatOps, recommended for the idea of chat as a shared command line where teammates learn by watching.

NSuaUok-wTY.summary: A LockPickingLawyer video in which a locksmith claims his videos are fake and challenges him; he responds by picking the lock. It is a short, typical LPL demonstration.
NSuaUok-wTY.why: Named as a favorite LPL video, where a skeptical locksmith's challenge gets answered quickly.

NV2yvI4Id9Q.summary: A clip of psychologist Jordan Peterson discussing why few women reach high-paying, high-pressure jobs. He talks about the tension between a demanding career and having a family.
NV2yvI4Id9Q.why: HN cites it in threads on gender gaps in tech and law, though some commenters point to a longer Peterson video for the full argument.

NVEgyJCTee4.summary: An ICFP 2015 keynote on the history of Standard ML, covering its ideas, principles and culture. It traces ML from Strachey, Landin and Milner through SML's development and its interplay with OCaml.
NVEgyJCTee4.why: Pointed to in language-history discussions as a good account of how ML and SML came to be.

NY66qpMFOYo.summary: ACS Reactions investigates why Mexican Coke, supposedly cane sugar sweetened, tested as having glucose and fructose, explaining that sucrose breaks down in acidic soda.
NY66qpMFOYo.why: Linked in corn syrup and Coca-Cola threads to show that sugar type barely matters in soda because sucrose inverts into the same sugars.

NYa8kirsUfg.summary: Giant Bomb interviews John Carmack at E3 2012 about his virtual reality head-mounted display prototype. He demos it and talks about latency, depth and focus problems in VR.
NYa8kirsUfg.why: HN links it as a primary source from the early days of modern VR, showing Carmack discussing his work before Oculus took off.

NZR_vMTLfIk.summary: A short Globe and Mail animated explainer on why renting can leave you as well off as buying a home. It walks through a rent-versus-buy comparison using Toronto numbers and the opportunity cost of a down payment. The video notes it dates from 2015 and the housing market has changed since.
NZR_vMTLfIk.why: HN commenters cite it as a clear, numbers-based rent-vs-buy comparison when housing-as-investment debates come up.

N_4R4X7AWtU.summary: Asianometry explains why Russia cannot replace TSMC after sanctions halted chip shipments. It looks at Russian chip designers such as Baikal, MCST and Yadro, and at Russia's lagging domestic manufacturing capacity.
N_4R4X7AWtU.why: HN recommends it in threads about sanctions and Russian military electronics, as an explanation of Russia's semiconductor limits.

Nbv9L-WIu0s.summary: Rusty Russell and Matt Evans examine why Unix utilities like ls and cat grew from a few kilobytes to over a hundred kilobytes. They take apart common tools to see where the growth comes from.
Nbv9L-WIu0s.why: Used in software bloat debates as a measured look at why binaries got larger.

NcUJnmBqHTY.summary: Pokey Rule presents Cursorless, a spoken language designed for editing code by voice, built on tree-sitter parsing with smart structural and simple token-level primitives. The talk is from Strange Loop 2023.
NcUJnmBqHTY.why: HN recommends it as the best overview of Cursorless, likened to vim with your voice, and relevant to accessibility and voice coding discussions.

NftT6HWFgq0.summary: Gary Bernhardt argues that software history moves in reactions to earlier tools, and that new tools are not simply better in every way. He distinguishes capability (what a tool allows) from suitability (what it fits), and warns against repeating past mistaken reactions.
NftT6HWFgq0.why: HN commenters reuse the capability-versus-suitability framing to discuss languages, restriction versus freedom, and tool design.

Nwew5gHoh3E.summary: An excerpt from Richard Dawkins's lecture on Climbing Mount Improbable demonstrating how a complex eye can evolve through incremental steps. It answers the creationist irreducible complexity argument.
Nwew5gHoh3E.why: HN uses it as the go-to rebuttal to irreducible complexity, showing that even simple photoreceptors are useful and stages exist in living animals.

NxvQPzrg2Wg.summary: A Kurzgesagt animated explainer on meat: why people love it and what it costs animals, the environment and health. It lays out the complicated trade-offs of meat production and consumption.
NxvQPzrg2Wg.why: Cited in animal-welfare and environmental threads as a short, thought-provoking piece on how humans treat animals.

NHWjlCaIrQo.summary: The climactic lesson scene from the 1983 film WarGames, in which the computer learns that the only winning move in nuclear war is not to play. It includes the character entering zero players and the famous closing line.
NHWjlCaIrQo.why: Mostly used as a joking or nostalgic reference in threads about nuclear war, AI and security exploits.

NJ7M01jV058.summary: Chubbyemu narrates the true case of a professor who spilled two drops of dimethylmercury on her hand and suffered fatal neurological damage.
NJ7M01jV058.why: Cited as the best accessible account of dimethylmercury poisoning, and as an example of the channel's grim medical case studies.

NM-zWTU7X-k.summary: A short clip of Richard Feynman on the difference between merely knowing how to reason mathematically and understanding why physical theories work. He discusses holding multiple equivalent ideas and guessing new laws.
NM-zWTU7X-k.why: HN uses it as a reference in threads on physics theories, models and what real understanding means.

NTfOnGZUZDk.summary: Brian Kernighan explains how grep came to be, written overnight by Ken Thompson, and how it got its name from the ed command g/re/p. He also covers the lineage from QED to ed that led to it.
NTfOnGZUZDk.why: HN commenters point to it as a short, charming first-hand account of Unix history from someone who was there.

NVAmnV65_zw.summary: Louis Rossmann argues that Apple designs and supports its products in ways that force planned obsolescence and obstruct independent repair. He draws on his experience repairing MacBooks and campaigns for right to repair.
NVAmnV65_zw.why: HN cites Rossmann for documentation of Apple's repair barriers, and some commenters credit him with changing their view of Apple. Others criticize the design choices he describes.

NbNFJK1ZpVg.summary: A former libertarian argues against libertarianism, describing the worst-case scenario if government disappeared overnight. It is drawn from the School Sucks Podcast episode on the natural state.
NbNFJK1ZpVg.why: Cited as a critique of libertarianism, including as a reply to the 'you can always leave' argument.

NdfmMB1E_qk.summary: Louis Rossmann explains why NYC commercial landlords keep storefronts vacant rather than lowering rents. He points to commercial mortgage-backed security loan terms and inflated property valuations.
NdfmMB1E_qk.why: HN uses it as the go-to explanation of why landlords refuse to renegotiate leases and leave units empty.

NfnWJUyUJYU.summary: The first lecture of Stanford's CS231n Winter 2016 course on convolutional neural networks for visual recognition, introducing the course and the historical context of computer vision.
NfnWJUyUJYU.why: HN lists it as a free, brilliant introduction to deep learning and computer vision, often within ML self-study plans.

Nyvxt1svxso.summary: A clip from George Carlin's 2005 special Life Is Worth Losing, in which he argues that the powerful don't want an educated public capable of critical thinking.
Nyvxt1svxso.why: Quoted whenever threads touch on elites, exclusivity and education, with 'it's a big club' as shorthand.

NMq0vncHJvU.summary: Martin Kleppmann's Local-First Conf talk reviewing where the local-first idea came from, where it stands five years after the essay, and what the community should work toward. He argues for generic sync infrastructure.
NMq0vncHJvU.why: Cited in sync-engine and local-first threads for Kleppmann's argument for a generic, standardised sync protocol or service.

NSDTZQdo6H8.summary: Andrej Karpathy's CVPR 2021 presentation on Tesla's Autopilot, covering its vision-based approach, sensor choices and the scale of Tesla's deep learning compute cluster. This upload is a lower-quality copy of the talk.
NSDTZQdo6H8.why: HN cites it as the primary source for Tesla's vision-only reasoning, LIDAR arguments and sensor fusion challenges.

NSaRb-iFwPA.summary: Rational Reminder podcast episode with Morgan Housel, author of The Psychology of Money. They discuss how investing success depends more on behavior than knowledge, the role of luck and the dangers of emulating top investors.
NSaRb-iFwPA.why: HN points to it as an interview with Housel and as the source of his quote that financial decisions happen at the dinner table, not on a spreadsheet.

NURiiQatBXA.summary: Chandler Carruth's GoingNative 2012 talk on Clang, covering how the compiler helps defend C++ code from mistakes. It makes the case for Clang's diagnostics and tooling.
NURiiQatBXA.why: Cited in discussions of why Clang exists and its case against GCC.

NUqytjlHNIM.summary: A one-minute clip from the 1966 film A Man for All Seasons. Thomas More refuses to arrest the Devil, saying he would give even the Devil the benefit of law for his own safety's sake.
NUqytjlHNIM.why: HN uses the scene to argue for due process and for protecting the speech and rights of people you dislike.

NV3sBlRgzTI.summary: A short excerpt of Elon Musk, interviewed by Kevin Rose, explaining first-principles reasoning with the example of the car versus improving horse carriages. He warns it takes much more mental energy than reasoning by analogy.
NV3sBlRgzTI.why: HN cites it as the standard illustration of reasoning from first principles, including his battery cost example.

NVVsdlHslfI.summary: A 13-minute clip from This Week in Startups in which Chamath Palihapitiya describes venture capital as a Ponzi-like scheme driven by fees and inflated valuations among VCs.
NVVsdlHslfI.why: Cited in threads about startups, VC and private equity as an insider's description of how VC economics work, though commenters note he is self-serving.

NWHfY_lvKIQ.summary: Joel Spolsky's 2009 Google Tech Talk on why StackOverflow was built, how it addresses the mess of searching for programming help, and the community design behind it. He also takes jabs at paywalled answer sites.
NWHfY_lvKIQ.why: Cited for Joel's account of how Stack Overflow's design and community thinking were figured out from the start.

Nbj1AR_aAcE.summary: A King's Politics interview with University of Chicago professor John Mearsheimer, recorded days before Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. He lays out the realist argument about NATO expansion and Russia's view of Ukraine.
Nbj1AR_aAcE.why: Cited during the 2022 invasion threads as the realist expert position on the Ukraine crisis, though some commenters see it as Russian apologism.

Ne1ApyqSvm0.summary: A Computer History Museum oral history with Bill Mensch, designer of the 6502 and 65816, covering his path from a Pennsylvania farm through Motorola and later work.
Ne1ApyqSvm0.why: Cited as a firsthand account of 6502 origins and of how engineers were treated at Motorola and Commodore.

NiTsduRreug.summary: A 15-minute clip of linguist Stephen Krashen discussing language acquisition, drawn from the 1980s. It presents his input hypothesis and the distinction between acquisition and learning.
NiTsduRreug.why: Cited as the source for comprehensible input, the principle behind immersion-based language learning methods and apps.

NlBjNmXvqIM.summary: A short clip of Steve Jobs explaining why Xerox failed to capitalize on its inventions. He says monopoly profits let sales and marketing people take over from product people.
NlBjNmXvqIM.why: Reached for constantly as the explanation for why dominant companies like Intel, Boeing and Blizzard stop innovating.

NqKyHEJe9_w.summary: A Computer History Museum demonstration with Dan Ingalls of Smalltalk-76 running on a Xerox Alto, recorded in 2017. He shows the live environment and discusses the system.
NqKyHEJe9_w.why: Used as a concrete example of live, REPL-driven Smalltalk environments and of what 1970s PARC computing looked like.

Nu-nlQqFCKg.summary: Microsoft Research's Rick Rashid demonstrates a speech recognition and translation system, built on deep neural networks, that turns his spoken English into Chinese speech in 2012.
Nu-nlQqFCKg.why: HN cites it as an early impressive real-time speech translation demo, often in discussions of voice-preserving translation and later AI demos.

NvDvESEXcgE.summary: Dialect coach Erik Singer analyzes how accurate the accents are of 32 well-known actors, including Brad Pitt and Will Smith, in WIRED's breakdown.
NvDvESEXcgE.why: HN finds Erik Singer's accent breakdowns informative and entertaining, and links them in discussions of accents and speech.

N1KvgtEnABY.summary: A three-minute clip from Dr. Strangelove in which Mandrake and Ripper (Peter Sellers and Sterling Hayden) discuss fluoridation and 'precious bodily fluids'. It is a famous Cold War satire scene.
N1KvgtEnABY.why: HN uses it as a joke reference whenever commenters mock conspiracy-minded worries about purity or poisoning; nobody recommends it as a video to learn from.

N3zU7sV4bJE.summary: A short video claiming that the chat app PiperChat violated COPPA, the US children's online privacy law, because it had no parental consent form. It says this led to a very large fine. It appears to be a clip from the TV show Silicon Valley.
N3zU7sV4bJE.why: HN mostly cites it as a humorous or illustrative reference to an extreme COPPA penalty.

N5xfBtD6rLY.summary: Pop Culture Detective examines how the US military works with Hollywood, using the Independence Day sequel's Army recruitment tie-in as the starting point. It looks at the joint marketing between 20th Century Fox and the military.
N5xfBtD6rLY.why: Cited in threads about military influence on movies and American cultural exports.

N6K9dS9wl7U.summary: A two-minute clip from 2008 in which Barack Obama states his position on same-sex marriage and civil unions. He says he supports civil unions rather than promoting same-sex marriage.
N6K9dS9wl7U.why: HN cites it as a record of Obama's 2008 stance, usually to make a point about how mainstream views on gay marriage shifted.

N9qYF9DZPdw.summary: Weird Al Yankovic's official music video for White & Nerdy, a parody of Chamillionaire's Ridin' about being a nerd.
N9qYF9DZPdw.why: Mostly invoked as a joke when nerd stereotypes come up, and once for a trivia card visible in the video.

N9wsjroVlu8.summary: The uncensored printer-smashing scene from the 1999 film Office Space.
N9wsjroVlu8.why: Posted as a joke or visual reference in threads about printers, office life and frustrating technology.

NCmTJkZy0rM.summary: A short film about the Dervaes family, who grow over 6,000 pounds of food a year on a tenth of an acre near downtown Los Angeles. They grow more than 400 plant species, keep chickens and ducks, and get most of their food from the plot.
NCmTJkZy0rM.why: HN cites it as proof of how much food a very small urban plot can produce.

NCvKXgp-Awo.summary: A corporate jingle-style song about KPMG, uploaded to YouTube with a glossy pop and R&B treatment. It is a cheesy corporate theme song.
NCvKXgp-Awo.why: Cited as a cringe-worthy example of corporate culture and bad corporate branding.

NDH3FDfVQl0.summary: A local TV news investigation showing that many SUVs and trucks have a large blind zone directly in front, hiding children from the driver. It includes a demonstration lining kids up in front of a vehicle.
NDH3FDfVQl0.why: HN cites it in threads about large vehicles and pedestrian safety as a vivid demonstration of front blind zones.

NH0aEp1oDOI.summary: Adobe's sneak-peek demo of Content-Aware Fill ahead of Photoshop CS5, showing objects being removed and areas repaired seamlessly with the delete key.
NH0aEp1oDOI.why: Referenced as the original demo that stunned people when object-removal and image-inpainting algorithms come up.

NIhCuzxNvv0.summary: A Thunderf00t video debunking Energy Vault, a gravity-based energy storage scheme that stacks concrete blocks with cranes. He argues it is impractical and compares it to pseudoscience.
NIhCuzxNvv0.why: Used as a critical reference to argue gravity energy storage is impractical, not as a general recommendation.

NK0Y9j_CGgM.summary: A short clip of Michio Kaku arguing that America's weak education system leaves a shortage of high-skilled tech workers, so H-1B visas bring in talent. It is an excerpt of a longer panel.
NK0Y9j_CGgM.why: Cited in immigration and STEM-talent debates as an authority's argument that H-1B is America's secret weapon.

NMQv0j29WHA.summary: A one-minute clip in which columnist John C. Dvorak explains to Dave Winer his technique for trolling the Apple community.
NMQv0j29WHA.why: HN cites it as proof that Dvorak writes inflammatory columns for clicks, to discredit his opinions.

NMS2VnDveP8.summary: A sketch from the Scottish comedy show Burnistoun in which two men cannot get a voice-recognition elevator to understand the word eleven in their accents.
NMS2VnDveP8.why: Used as a joke whenever voice interfaces and accents come up, and shared as a Scottish comedy sample.

NPTzNJMd19A.summary: AvE tears down a broken Dyson Animal vacuum and its expensive replacement, criticizing the molded plastic, flimsy switches and overall engineering, with his usual profane commentary.
NPTzNJMd19A.why: HN cites it as a detailed teardown of a Dyson vacuum showing little substance beneath the branding.

NSNXBvpLb9o.summary: A CNN segment showing William Shatner emotionally describing his Blue Origin suborbital flight to Jeff Bezos right after landing.
NSNXBvpLb9o.why: HN mentions it mostly critically, calling the clip clickbait, or to point out how early the Bezos moment occurs.

NT7_SxJ3oSI.summary: A Ryan George comedy sketch about the experience of using Google search in 2022, where results are full of ads, spam and Reddit and Amazon detours.
NT7_SxJ3oSI.why: HN links it as a joke about the decline of Google search, as comedy that captures a widely shared frustration.

NU-fTr-udZg.summary: Ted Young of LightStep proposes trace testing, using distributed tracing data to unify testing and observability. The KubeCon-era talk argues for testing against trace data rather than treating tests and monitoring separately.
NU-fTr-udZg.why: Mostly linked by a company in its recurring hiring posts as a tech talk showing its approach, rather than recommended by commenters.

NYJ2w82WifU.summary: A short clip from the comedy film The Dictator in which a doctor delivers a test result in a running gag around the name Aladeen.
NYJ2w82WifU.why: HN uses it only as a joke reference in unrelated threads.

NcZxaFfxloo.summary: Jon Stewart interviews Ezra Klein about his book Abundance and why progressive goals get stuck in procedure and regulation. They discuss how to streamline government and what could be built without bureaucratic obstacles.
NcZxaFfxloo.why: Cited as a source of examples such as California high-speed rail and rural broadband subsidies when HN discusses government dysfunction.

NgHFMolXs3U.summary: A short pre-recorded talk by Rich Sutton for the World AI Conference in Shanghai arguing that succession from humanity to AI is inevitable. He lays out his view of that transition.
NgHFMolXs3U.why: Cited critically, as evidence of the unsettling perspective of a prominent AI researcher who seems to accept humanity being replaced.

NjpNG0CJRMM.summary: Sam Altman accepts the 2023 Hawking Fellowship at the Cambridge Union and speaks about OpenAI, AGI and AI safety, recorded November 1, 2023. It includes his comments on what is left for AGI and on discovering new physics.
NjpNG0CJRMM.why: During the Altman ouster threads, HN mined it for his recent unscripted statements on AGI and safety; some also mock its tone.

NlHUz99l-eo.summary: A 2006 iPod commercial set to Daft Punk's Technologic, with dancing silhouettes and bright white headphones.
NlHUz99l-eo.why: Cited as an example of Apple selling feelings and status rather than specs.

Nl_Qyk9DSUw.summary: A short clip of Lucille Bluth from Arrested Development asking how much a banana could cost.
Nl_Qyk9DSUw.why: HN uses it as a joke reply about underestimating costs.

NoAzpa1x7jU.summary: The final scene of Blade Runner (Final Cut) in which Roy Batty delivers the Tears in Rain monologue. It is a short film clip.
NoAzpa1x7jU.why: HN mostly quotes or links it as a cultural reference, often as a joke or tribute, rather than recommending it.

NuAMczraBIM.summary: A Motherboard documentary on Rich, who buys wrecked Teslas, rebuilds them from salvaged parts and shares the process as Rich Rebuilds. It shows the obstacles to repairing cars Tesla won't service.
NuAMczraBIM.why: HN cites it in right-to-repair and EV battery discussions as an example of independent Tesla repair.

NwVBzx0LMNQ.summary: A short compilation of the gesture and multitouch interface scenes from the film Minority Report.
NwVBzx0LMNQ.why: Cited in discussions of sci-fi interfaces and whether ideas like pinch-to-zoom were prior art.

NzaRVEzYuz8.summary: A short walkthrough of a hack that tricks a Brother laser printer into accepting third-party toner by working around its genuine-toner check. It notes this may void the warranty.
NzaRVEzYuz8.why: Linked in printer DRM threads as proof that workarounds exist for Brother's cartridge restrictions.

NztgXMLwv4A.summary: A Polish linguist tests whether speakers of Bulgarian, Polish and Croatian can understand Interslavic, a constructed language built from Slavic languages. It shows how well they follow it without prior study.
NztgXMLwv4A.why: HN points to it as a striking demonstration that Interslavic works for speakers of different Slavic languages.
